principles: Customer authentication policy is scoped to the ACME LOS customer group, not Okta Everyone.
App access policy is assigned only to ACME LOS web and mobile apps.
Org authenticator activation, Okta risk scoring, device assurance, and device signal collection are Okta org features; ACME scopes their use through customer-group and app rules where Okta allows it.
IDX passwords, security-question answers, and OTPs are sent directly from the browser to Okta; MyAccount password-change values pass transiently through the BFF and are never logged or persisted.
Security questions are reserved for account recovery, following Okta's recommendation not to use them for routine authentication.
Backend profile sync happens only after a fresh ACME session.

hierarchy.label: Org Authenticators
hierarchy.purpose: Activate or disable the Okta authenticators the customer policies can reference.

hierarchy.label: Device And Risk Signals
hierarchy.purpose: Provides Okta risk, anomalous-device, device assurance, and device signal-collection inputs that app sign-in rules can consume when the org supports them.

hierarchy.label: Email As Username
hierarchy.purpose: Keeps self-service registration simple by mapping the customer's primary email to the Okta login attribute.

hierarchy.label: Customer Group
hierarchy.purpose: Holds self-service ACME LOS customer users and keeps customer policy away from admin users.

hierarchy.label: Profile Enrollment
hierarchy.purpose: Registers new customers and targets them into the customer group.

hierarchy.label: Authenticator Enrollment
hierarchy.purpose: Requires the customer authenticators needed for sign-in and recovery.

hierarchy.label: Global Session
hierarchy.purpose: Controls customer Okta session lifetime, idle timeout, and remember-device behavior.

hierarchy.label: App Sign-In
hierarchy.purpose: Controls ACME LOS web/mobile app sign-in and risk-based step-up.

hierarchy.label: Authorization Server
hierarchy.purpose: Issues ACME claims and tokens for scoped customer app access.

hierarchy.label: Account Management
hierarchy.purpose: Controls supported password and authenticator recovery operations. MyAccount email, phone, and password APIs are outside this policy.

hierarchy.label: ACME Backend Sync
hierarchy.purpose: Enforces fresh proof, calls user-scoped MyAccount APIs, and syncs mutable profile data only after Okta has re-authenticated the user.

scenarios.title: New Customer Registration
flow: Customer starts app-owned IDX registration from the ACME sign-in surface.
Okta IDX profile enrollment captures email as the login identifier, first name, last name, and visible State backed by the acmeState Missouri/Texas dropdown, then targets {customerGroupName}.
Authenticator enrollment requires password, email, security question, and phone/SMS in dev when telephony is enabled; the app renders only the IDX remediation inputs returned by Okta.
Phone is captured once during Okta phone/SMS authenticator enrollment; ACME does not also collect profile phone on the registration profile form.
securityNotes: Admin users should not be members of {customerGroupName}.
Registration policy must not be scoped to Okta Everyone.
Password validation, security-question answer, and OTP material stay in Okta.

scenarios.title: Standard Sign-In
flow: Customer signs in through the app-owned IDX surface for web or the mobile OIDC app.
Global session policy applies to {customerGroupName} with a {sessionLifetimeDays}-day maximum session lifetime.
Okta evaluates the global-session primary authenticator and the ACME app access policy; the web BFF redeems the Interaction Code and creates an opaque session.
Authorization server issues ACME claims for the scoped customer app session.
securityNotes: Browser receives only the opaque ACME session cookie.
Okta tokens remain server-side in the ACME session store.

scenarios.title: High-Risk And New-Device Sign-In
flow: Okta evaluates the ACME web/mobile app sign-in risk rule.
New user, new-device, and anomalous-device signals can contribute to Okta sign-in risk when the org supports those signals.
High-risk access requires password-first 2FA without requiring a security-question challenge/hint during sign-in.
Standard access remains lower priority.
securityNotes: The ACCESS_POLICY is assigned only to ACME LOS web and mobile apps.
Bootstrap logs a warning if the Okta org does not accept the adaptive risk rule.
Device assurance and device signal collection are Okta org features; when required, verify the org feature and the app-rule consumption manually.

scenarios.title: Forgot Password: Security Question + Phone/SMS OTP
flow: Customer chooses forgot password from the app-owned IDX sign-in page.
Okta account management or password recovery policy verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Okta sends a phone/SMS OTP before reset when telephony is enabled.
Customer sets a new password in Okta.
Okta signs the customer out or ACME treats any existing session as stale.
Customer must establish a fresh ACME sign-in with the new password.
securityNotes: ACME never receives the old password, new password, security-question answer, or SMS OTP.
This scenario must be scoped to {customerGroupName}; admin users are out of scope.
Bootstrap manages the Okta account-management policy rule through the public Policy API.
oktaSurfaces: Security > Authenticators > Password > Rules > Recovery authenticators

scenarios.title: Change Email
flow: Customer starts change email from the read-only ACME account dashboard.
App-owned IDX requires fresh password reauthentication and phone/SMS OTP before the change UI opens.
The BFF validates subject continuity, proof age, assurance, and password plus SMS authentication methods before calling the user-scoped MyAccount Email API.
The customer explicitly requests a verification code for the new email, enters it on the same page, and ACME aligns the Okta login only after verification succeeds.
ACME requires the customer to sign out after the change.
Customer signs in again with the new email and satisfies email OTP.
ACME syncs backend email from the current Okta email claim when Okta subject is unchanged.
securityNotes: Okta Account Management Policy does not protect the MyAccount Email API; the ACME BFF guard is authoritative.
ACME logs the email-change event without logging old or new email values, OTPs, tokens, or passwords.

scenarios.title: Change Password
flow: Customer starts change password from the ACME account-security page while signed in.
App-owned IDX requires fresh password reauthentication and phone/SMS OTP before the change page opens.
The BFF validates subject continuity, proof age, assurance, and password plus SMS authentication methods before the mutation.
ACME BFF forwards the current and new password to Okta MyAccount without storing either value.
ACME requires the customer to sign out after the change.
Customer signs in again with the new password.
securityNotes: Okta Account Management Policy does not protect the MyAccount Password API; the ACME BFF guard is authoritative.
ACME does not store, log, sync, or reuse old password, new password, or OTP.
Security question remains in the Okta-managed forgot-password recovery flow. Okta recommends against using security questions in routine authentication.
The same active Okta session is not enough for ACME profile sync after the password change.

scenarios.title: Lost Phone: Replace SMS Factor
flow: Customer reports a lost phone or unavailable SMS factor; email remains the sign-in identifier.
Okta verifies email OTP before allowing recovery to continue.
Okta verifies the enrolled security-question challenge/hint.
Okta allows the customer to replace the phone/SMS factor after proof succeeds.
Okta may show only a masked prior phone hint when useful; do not reveal the full prior phone number.
Customer signs in fresh with the unchanged email and the new phone/SMS OTP after phone/SMS factor replacement.
ACME treats verified phone as Okta-owned until a trusted claim, Management API lookup, or event hook is enabled.
securityNotes: This scenario is not live until Okta phone/SMS is enabled or another non-phone possession factor is configured.
Do not use the unavailable phone factor as its own recovery proof.
Phone is not the ACME sign-in identifier; this is factor replacement, not sign-in identifier recovery.

scenarios.title: Change Phone/SMS
flow: Customer starts change phone from the read-only ACME account dashboard.
App-owned IDX requires fresh password reauthentication and email OTP before the change UI opens.
The BFF validates subject continuity, proof age, assurance, and password plus email authentication methods before calling the user-scoped MyAccount Phone API.
The customer explicitly requests a code for the new phone and enters it on the same page.
ACME requires the customer to sign out after the change.
Customer signs in fresh with the unchanged email and the new phone/SMS OTP after the phone/SMS change.
The dashboard reads the verified phone from the user-scoped MyAccount Phone API.
securityNotes: Okta Account Management Policy does not protect the MyAccount Phone API; the ACME BFF guard is authoritative.
Phone/SMS remains demo-only through the dev mock provider until real carrier SMS is approved.
ACME does not claim an application servicing phone number is the verified Okta SMS factor.

scenarios.title: Fresh ACME Sign-In After Sensitive Change
flow: Sensitive MyAccount action completes.
The success dialog requires server-side sign-out through the Okta end-session endpoint.
Customer signs in again through the app-owned IDX page.
ACME syncs only non-secret profile data from fresh token claims.
securityNotes: Do not sync password material, OTPs, or security-question material.

scenarios.title: Customer ID Sample Writeback
flow: Customer saves ACME personal information.
Next validates the browser session and forwards trusted identity to the internal BFF.
BFF uses Okta Management OAuth service-app credentials to patch a sample customerId when missing.
BFF updates the current ACME Redis auth-session metadata with the effective customerId when the session does not already have one.
Future token refresh or sign-in receives the customerId claim from Okta.
securityNotes: Okta management private key is BFF-only through Key Vault or environment secret.
ACME updates only derived session metadata; it never mutates the signed Okta JWT stored with the session.
This sample bridge is dev-only until the real customer-id issuer exists.

manualChecks.title: Admin users are not in the ACME customer group
Forgot password requires security question plus phone/SMS OTP and fresh sign-in
IDX registration requires email login identifier, first name, last name, and acmeState Missouri/Texas dropdown
Org setting maps primary email to login attribute for self-service registration
Org Embedded widget sign-in support has Interaction Code enabled
Customer global session policy has a 60-day maximum lifetime and 120-minute idle timeout
Adaptive high-risk/new-device sign-in is assigned only to ACME web and mobile apps and does not require security-question answer at sign-in
Org-level authenticator, risk, device assurance, and device signal features are explicitly documented when they cannot be app-scoped
BFF-enforced email/password changes use phone/SMS OTP and phone changes use email OTP before MyAccount mutation
